description: Undoing the wound rather than closing it - a healer whose mending runs long and whose Aeons reshape it.
_source_note: Rebuilt 6 Nov 2026 from the 38 real CoA Time talents (role HEALER). Building it uncovered and prompted a fix to the HoT duration bug: the HoT branch divided a fixed total by the TALENTED duration, so every heal-over-time extension talent in the game was making healers worse. CoA's Time tree is full of them, so they are the backbone here and now pay properly, through the new hot_duration_pct key and the per-ability _duration keys. on_heal_cast passes the CASTER and never the healed ally, so every CoA talent of the form 'healing done by X applies Y to the target' is turned around to the caster side. The four Aeon/Fabric unlocks are load-bearing and asserted.

nodes.name: Sands of Life
nodes.description: Increases your healing power by 12% of your Spirit.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases your healing power by 25% of your Spirit.' PORTS EXACTLY - healing_power is in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS and spirit in STAT_CONVERSION_SOURCES. Was a pure scalar on our side. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Patient Mending
nodes.description: Increases the duration of your heal over time effects by 21%.
nodes._source: Stands in for CoA's shared-tree Eternal ('Increases the duration of your Accelerated Recovery by 6 sec and Decomposition by 3 sec') as this tree's entry point, because duration is what the spec is about and because hot_duration_pct did not exist until 6 Nov 2026. It is the healing companion to dot_duration_pct, and it only became worth authoring once the HoT branch stopped dividing the total by the talented duration - before that fix this node would have made a healer strictly worse. Per-turn healing now derives from the ability's own base duration, so +20% duration is +20% total healing at full per-tick value. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Time Wizard
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Reverse Wound, Epoch and Correct the Mistake by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases the critical strike chance of your Reverse Wound, Epoch, and Correct the Mistake by 8%.' PORTS EXACTLY, all three abilities, using per-ability crit keys rather than a global so the node stays the one CoA wrote. Per-ability crit keys are in PERCENTAGE POINTS. Was a pure scalar on our side. NOTE for anyone reading this later: heals CAN crit, but HoTs cannot - 'heals and DoTs never roll crit' in the palette notes refers to periodic ticks, so these three (two direct heals and a party heal) are the right targets and Accelerated Recovery would not have been.

nodes.name: Timeless
nodes.description: Reduces the mana cost of your healing spells by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'While Endless Sands is active, the mana costs of your spells and abilities is reduced by -3% per stack.' Both conditions fail - nothing reads whether another effect is active, and nothing reads a stack count - so this becomes the unconditional version at a flat 10%. heal_cost_pct is live (abilities.py:1226), is a FRACTION, and POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Carbon Dating
nodes.description: Increases the healing of Epoch by 12%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Each stack of Sands of Time now also increases the healing of your Epoch by 10%.' The per-stack scaling is unbuildable (nothing reads a stack count), so it lands as a flat 20% on the same ability - which is what CoA's two stacks amount to. Was a pure scalar on our side. A FRACTION.

nodes.name: Fabric of Time
nodes.description: Teaches Fabric of Time, reaching back to undo an ally's wound.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Alter the fabric of time, healing an ally. Your next Aeon used within 8 sec will trigger with no cooldown or cost.' LOAD-BEARING UNLOCK - chronomancer_fabric_of_time carries requires_talent and this is its only unlock node; dropping it makes the ability unobtainable forever. The 'next Aeon is free' clause lives on the ability, not here; nothing waives a resource cost from a talent.

nodes.name: Keep Accelerating
nodes.description: Your healing spells have a 35% chance to also mend your most wounded ally for 25% of the amount healed.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Accelerated Recovery now also applies to the lowest-health nearby target.' A talent cannot add a target to an ability, and a HoT fires no on_heal_cast at all (it goes through the dot/hot branch, which appends no heal event), so keying off Accelerated Recovery specifically is doubly impossible. Built instead as a smart heal off the spec's direct heals: smart_heal_pct is one of only three payloads that READ the triggering amount, and it picks the worst-off ally, which is exactly CoA's 'lowest-health nearby target'. The ability it keys off changed; the behaviour it produces did not. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: Aeon of Protection
nodes.description: Teaches Aeon of Protection, turning Epoch into a shield against what is coming.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases Epoch's cast time by 15%, healing done by 15%, and causes it to apply a damage absorption shield equal to 30% of the amount healed for 8 sec. Shares a cooldown with other Aeon spells.' LOAD-BEARING UNLOCK. There is no shared-cooldown mechanism and no cast times, but the ability already exists in our data carrying its own effects, so this node is the unlock and nothing else - which is the right shape for a mode-switch talent anyway.

nodes.name: Aeon of Renewal
nodes.description: Teaches Aeon of Renewal, trading Epoch's burst for healing that keeps arriving.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces Epoch's healing by 30%, but causes it to heal for an additional 50% of the amount healed over 3 sec. Healing done by this ability cannot critically hit.' LOAD-BEARING UNLOCK. The cannot-crit clause is free here: HoT ticks never roll crit in this engine regardless, so CoA's own restriction is already the behaviour.

nodes.name: Cadence of Time
nodes.description: Your critical heals increase your healing done by 8% for 5 turns, stacking up to 5 times.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your critical strikes with Epoch now grant Cadence of Time, increasing the healing of Ripple by 10% for 15 seconds. Stacks 5 times.' The two ability scopings both go - there is no per-ability proc trigger, and a status effect cannot carry a per-ability healing key - so it becomes a general healing buff off critical heals, keeping CoA's 5 stacks and its 'crit feeds the next heal' loop. max_stacks is real; nothing can READ the count, but the effect genuinely stacks. CAREFUL: healing_power_pct is PERCENTAGE POINTS (character.py:1295 divides by 100), so 8 is 8% - and it sits twelve lines from max_mana_pct, which is read raw as a fraction. 15 sec -> 5 turns. Was a pure scalar on our side.

nodes.name: A Ripple In Time
nodes.description: Your critical heals have a 40% chance to reduce the cooldown of Ripple by 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your damaging and healing critical strikes now reduce the remaining cooldown of Ripple by 1 sec.' PORTS ALMOST EXACTLY - on_crit covers both damaging and healing crits, and reset_cooldown with an {abilities, turns} dict shaves turns rather than resetting outright (a bare list resets fully). 1 sec -> 2 turns because a 1-second shave on a 30-second cooldown is proportionally about two turns off ten, and a sub-turn reduction would round to nothing.

nodes.name: Time Beacon
nodes.description: Increases the duration of Accelerated Recovery by 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA over 2 ranks: 'Increases the duration of effects applied by your Aeons by 4 sec.' The Aeon scoping cannot be built (nothing reads which Aeon is active, and the Aeons' effects live on their own abilities), so it is pointed at the spec's actual HoT. 4 sec -> 3 turns, close enough at ~3 sec per turn given Accelerated Recovery runs 7. THIS NODE WOULD HAVE BEEN A TRAP BEFORE 6 Nov 2026: the HoT branch divided its fixed total by the talented duration, so +3 turns meant the same healing spread thinner - Accelerated Recovery measured 7 turns x 29 (203 total) unmodified and 11 x 18 (198) with a +4 talent. Now per-turn derives from the base duration and this is +3 ticks at full value. A SMALL INTEGER IN TURNS, so talent_ranks.spread() refuses to rank it - which is correct; a per-rank duration of one turn is the smallest unit there is.

nodes.name: Aeon of Oblivion
nodes.description: Teaches Aeon of Oblivion, spending mana to make Epoch land harder.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases Epoch's mana cost by 30%, critical strike chance by 10%, and healing done by 15%. In addition, healing with Epoch now increases the target's damage dealt by 3% for 15 sec.' LOAD-BEARING UNLOCK. CoA puts this effect ON THE HEALED ALLY, which no talent can do. on_heal_cast passes the CASTER, not the recipient (recorded in the project's talent palette notes and verified), and the only payload that reaches an ally at all is a smart heal, which heals the worst-off ally but cannot buff them. Turned around to the caster side so the node does something real; the tooltip states the caster-side version rather than promising an ally buff that never lands. In this case the ally-damage clause is simply dropped rather than turned around, because a healer buffing their own damage is not what the Aeon is for; the ability's own stat changes carry the node.

nodes.name: Shield of the Ages
nodes.description: When a critical strike hits you, your damage taken is reduced by 3% and healing you receive is increased by 5% for 3 turns, stacking up to 3 times.
nodes._source: CoA: 'When hit by a damaging critical strike, your damage taken is reduced by 3%, and healing received is increased by 5% for 3 sec, stacking 3 times.' PORTS ALMOST EXACTLY. The 'critical' filter is dropped: on_damage_taken gets no attacker and no ability_id from monsters, so there is nothing to test crit against. 3 sec -> 3 turns. KEPT AS A WORKED EXAMPLE OF THE PROJECT'S UNIT TRAP - the two keys in this one stat_mods dict read in DIFFERENT units. damage_taken_pct is RAW on both sides (character.py:2697 adds the status mod with no division), so -0.03 is -3%; authoring -3 would be -300% damage taken, which heals the player on every hit. healing_taken_pct is PERCENTAGE POINTS in a status effect (character.py:2904 divides by 100), so 5 is +5%; authoring 0.05 would deliver 0.05%. Both asserted in main().

nodes.name: Orderly Protector
nodes.description: Your healing spells have a 20% chance to reset the cooldown of Fabric of Time.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Healing done by your Epoch now increases the healing of Fabric of Time by 10% for 10 sec, stacking 10 times. Each stack gives you a 2% chance when you cast Fabric of Time to reset its own cooldown.' The stacking buff and the per-stack chance both need a readable stack count, which does not exist, so the two clauses collapse into the one that can be built: a flat chance on heal to reset Fabric of Time outright. A BARE LIST resets fully, unlike the {abilities, turns} form used elsewhere in this tree - that is the whole difference between the two and it is easy to type the wrong one. 1-turn ICD so it cannot chain off a single turn's healing.

nodes.name: Chronicler
nodes.description: Increases the duration of your heal over time effects by a further 24% and their healing by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Fortify Timeline now extends the duration of Accelerated Recovery on all targets within 40 yds by an additional 10 sec.' There is no positioning and no per-ability proc trigger, and extending an effect already on OTHER targets is impossible (no payload extends a live effect's duration), so this becomes the global version. Stacks additively with Patient Mending for 45% longer HoTs on a healer who takes both. MIXED UNITS ON PURPOSE AND BOTH CORRECT: hot_duration_pct is a FRACTION (0.25 = +25%) while healing_power_pct is PERCENTAGE POINTS (15 = +15%), because character.py:1295 divides the latter by 100 and abilities.py reads the former raw. Asserted in main().

nodes.name: Shimmering Shard
nodes.description: Your spells have a 30% chance to increase your damage and healing by 5% for 6 turns, stacking up to 3 times.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Activating Aeon spells now grants you 4% increased damage and healing for 20 sec, stacking 3 times.' The Aeon scoping goes (no per-ability proc trigger) and becomes on_cast at 30%, which fires on any spell and keeps the stacking window meaningful. 20 sec -> 6 turns, CoA's 3 stacks kept. ANOTHER CORRECTED 5 Nov 2026, PARTIALLY: this dict carried all_damage, which is NOT readable from a status effect. The damage path reads all_damage through get_talent_effect (abilities.py:1606-1610), which sums talents and the current stance ONLY; a status effect's stat_mods go to get_status_stat_mod, from which the damage path reads exactly one key - damage_dealt_pct, in PERCENTAGE POINTS (abilities.py:1680-1683). So that half was silent dead data. healing_power_pct is KEPT: it was briefly changed too, on the mistaken assumption that it shared the problem, and then MEASURED - it moves healing_power on a live character, because _recalculate_derived_stats folds status effects into the same `bonuses` pool as gear (character.py:1218). Reverted. audit_talents could not see the all_damage half because that key HAS read sites, just not from a status effect, which is the blind spot tools/qa_proc_stat_mods.py now closes. Was a pure scalar on our side before any of this.

nodes.name: Cycling Aeons
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of your Aeons by 39%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the cooldown of your Aeons by -50%.' Built literally, one key per Aeon, because there is no ability-group concept to address all three at once. 50% -> 40% because these are mode switches and a Chronomancer flipping Aeon every other turn is not the rotation CoA describes. *_cooldown_pct keys are FRACTIONS and POSITIVE MEANS A REDUCTION, which is the opposite sign convention from most of the file and has caught this project before. talented_cooldown floors at 1 turn, so stacked reductions cannot make these spammable.

nodes.name: Timeline Tether
nodes.description: Your healing spells have a 30% chance to reduce the cooldown of Fortify Timeline by 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your periodic damage and healing reduces the cooldown of your Fortify Timeline by 1 sec.' CoA hangs this off PERIODIC TICKS, which are not a trigger: status_effects.py:914 ticks a dot or hot by calling the recipient's own take_damage/heal with no caster reference, so there is nobody to fire a proc on. Re-pointed to on_heal_cast, which is the closest live trigger for a healer and keeps the node's purpose - heal often, get Fortify Timeline back sooner. This is the same loss Infinite takes seven times over, and it is the class's defining translation gap.

nodes.name: Mark of Order
nodes.description: Increases your healing done by 6% and the healing of Reverse Wound by a further 12%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Healing done by Fortify Timeline now applies Mark of Order. Mark of Order increases the healing of your next Reverse Wound on the target by 10% for 20 sec. Every 1 sec for the duration, they gain an additional stack, up to 5.' CoA puts this effect ON THE HEALED ALLY, which no talent can do. on_heal_cast passes the CASTER, not the recipient (recorded in the project's talent palette notes and verified), and the only payload that reaches an ally at all is a smart heal, which heals the worst-off ally but cannot buff them. Turned around to the caster side so the node does something real; the tooltip states the caster-side version rather than promising an ally buff that never lands. The per-second stack accrual is separately impossible - there is no periodic or tick trigger of any kind. Turned around to a flat caster-side pair that produces the same outcome in play (Reverse Wound lands harder), at roughly what CoA's five stacks come to. Was a pure scalar on our side. healing_power_pct is PERCENTAGE POINTS, the ability key is a FRACTION.

nodes.name: Overcorrection
nodes.description: Your healing spells have a 30% chance to leave a mending that heals you over 4 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Overhealing done by Correct the Mistake now applies a heal over time effect to the ally equal to 30% of the healing done over 5 seconds.' Three separate gaps: nothing measures OVERHEALING (the heal path returns the amount healed, not the surplus); there is no per-ability proc trigger; and CoA puts this effect ON THE HEALED ALLY, which no talent can do. on_heal_cast passes the CASTER, not the recipient (recorded in the project's talent palette notes and verified), and the only payload that reaches an ally at all is a smart heal, which heals the worst-off ally but cannot buff them. Turned around to the caster side so the node does something real; the tooltip states the caster-side version rather than promising an ally buff that never lands. So it becomes a self-mending HoT off any heal, which keeps the node's shape (heal a lot, get a trailing heal) while being honest about who receives it. 5 sec -> 4 turns. A proc-applied hot carries `potency` as its PER-TURN healing, unlike an ability rank's effect_value, which is the TOTAL across the duration and gets divided - so 18 here is 18 per turn, 72 over the effect.

nodes.name: Titan's Gaze
nodes.description: Reduces all damage you take by 6% and increases your maximum health by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Time Out! no longer breaks on damage, but now only reduces damage taken by 15%.' Time Out! is a channel and nothing controls whether an effect breaks on damage, so the node is rebuilt as the passive survivability a healer actually needs, at the mitigation CoA's own clause names. Folded in CoA's Nozdormu's Gaze, which also modifies Time Out! and is unbuildable for the same reason. CAREFUL, TWO CONVENTIONS IN ONE DICT AND BOTH DELIBERATE: as a TALENT effect damage_taken_pct is read RAW (character.py:2696, so -0.06 is -6%) and max_health_pct is a FRACTION too - but inside a STATUS EFFECT max_health_pct becomes percentage points and damage_taken_pct stays raw, so the pair flips apart depending on where it is written. These are talent effects, so both are fractions.

nodes.name: The Vast Infinite
nodes.description: Increases the duration of your heal over time effects by a further 35%, your healing done by 11%, and your healing spells have a 40% chance to mend your most wounded ally for 35% of the amount healed.
nodes._source: CoA: 'All party and raid members become one, equally sharing 25% of all damage dealt to them for 10 sec, up to a maximum of 100% of their total health. At the end of the duration, all affected allies are healed equal to the total damage shared split evenly amongst all allies.' NOT BUILDABLE, and for a reason this project has hit three times now: there is no accumulator or deferred-damage pool anywhere in the engine - the same gap that killed Puppeteer's Threads, Oathkeeper and Base: Beast Blood - and no trigger fires on an effect expiring. The ABILITY of the same name exists in our data, is ungated, and is left exactly as authored; this node is the capstone the tree has actually been building toward. hot_duration_pct here takes a Chronomancer who also has Patient Mending and Chronicler to +80% HoT duration, which on a 7-turn Accelerated Recovery is 13 turns at full per-tick value - the healer mirror of Infinite's long dots, and only honest at all since the HoT branch was fixed on 6 Nov 2026. The smart heal is the one payload that genuinely reaches an ally and picks the worst-off one, which is the nearest thing in the engine to 'all party members become one'.

nodes.name: Compounded Moment
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike damage of your spells by 20% per rank.
nodes._source: Authored 6 Nov. Kyle: 'all caster classes should have a 5 point talent that increases their spell crit damage by 100%.' Mirrors priest_shadow's Shadow Power and shaman_elemental's Elemental Fury, both of which are WoW-accurate at 5 x 20%. Placed on tier 4 beside the existing tier-4 block; connected_to is cosmetic (it draws the edge), spending is gated by tier_requirements.
